evals.prompt: I want to improve the google-sheets skill. It's making too many API calls - I counted around 45 calls to write a simple spreadsheet. Can we get that down to under 30? Start the improvement process.
evals.expected_output: Creates workspace, discovers metrics from skill output, asks user which metrics to optimize, saves config.json with optimization_goals containing api_call_count <= 30

assertions.text: Locates and references the google-sheets skill
Identifies api_call_count or similar as the metric to optimize
Sets target of <= 30 for the metric

evals.prompt: The website-qc skill is slow - takes about 3 minutes to QC a 10-page site. I want to speed it up. Also track if we introduce any new false positives (issue_count shouldn't go up). Initialize skill-improver for this.
evals.expected_output: Creates workspace, identifies wall_time_seconds as primary metric to minimize, issue_count as secondary metric to prevent regression, asks for test cases or uses skill's evals.json

assertions.text: Identifies wall_time or speed as primary metric to optimize
Identifies issue_count as secondary metric for regression tracking
Locates and references the website-qc skill
Proposes a structured improvement approach rather than ad-hoc changes

evals.prompt: Continue improving the skill in skill-improver-workspace. Run 2 more iterations. Last time we tried batching and it worked, so maybe try caching next.
evals.expected_output: Reads existing config.json and heuristics.md, generates 2 hypotheses (one about caching), runs experiments, evaluates results, updates heuristics.md with learnings, appends to results.tsv

assertions.text: Checks for existing workspace/config before proceeding
Generates hypothesis in structured format (problem, change, expected improvement)
Proposes changing ONE thing per iteration, not multiple
References prior learning (batching worked) in new hypothesis
